speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) what are the trends of youths radicalising via gaming, chat and social media platforms; and (b) what are the steps taken to strengthen the tracking and identification of extremist messaging and ideologies on such platforms.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: They were exposed to extremist and radical content through a variety of online platforms, including gaming, chat and social media platforms.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Government has blocked access to some websites that perpetuate extremist messaging and ideologies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: As announced during the Ministry of Communications and Information (MCI)'s Committee of Supply debate this year, MCI will study further measures to strengthen online safety on other services, including gaming platforms and app stores.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: But despite our best efforts, it is not possible to block all extremist content, given the vastness of the Internet.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: New extremist content and new sites are constantly popping up.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Determined individuals will find ways to circumvent our blocking.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We have therefore been working with community partners, such as the Religious Rehabilitation Group (RRG) and Inter-Agency Aftercare Group (ACG), on outreach efforts to strengthen the community's resilience to extremist ideologies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The public, particularly family members and friends, also play an important role.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: They can seek help for someone close to them whom they are concerned has been radicalised, or report suspicious behaviour by calling the ISD Counter-Terrorism Centre hotline at 1800-262 6473; or 999; SMS to 7199; or using the "Report" function in the SGSecure app.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The identity of the informer will be protected.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Early reporting will allow the authorities to intervene quickly to avert a tragedy, including to the radicalised person.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: If the person is only in the early stages of radicalisation, he or she may simply be referred for counselling and may not need to be detained under the ISA.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I think the Minister of State for his response.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: What is MHA's our overall engagement strategy to counter radicalisation especially for youths, for example, by engaging some of the stakeholders.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Specifically, can the Ministry give further details of how it is working with families of these youths to prevent radicalisation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Indeed, MHA, specifically ISD, have been working with other Government agencies and community partners to reach out to different segments in the community, to raise public awareness of the threat of terrorism and online radicalisation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, such upstream efforts are important, preventing radical ideology on taking root in our society.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: This is especially important for youths, who are impressionable and more easily influenced.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: They also have visits to the RRG resource counselling centres, we did online engagement during COVID-19 and we also reached out to the youth and families via physical engagements after we have recovered from COVID-19.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: For example, the RRG arranged a visit to ISD Heritage Centre for 50 youths and we also engage youths of Indian Muslim Social Service Association.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: At the end of the day, we will continue this journey.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We have been engaging families, youths and as many people as we would like and are able to.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Recently, we engaged a group of religious leaders and we are happy that they are more than willing to help us in this effort.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: What is key is that, as I shared in the MHA's Committee of Supply, we will continue to enhance our operational capabilities and our outreach efforts.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In fact, this Thursday, I am engaging another group of stakeholders as part of the counter-terrorism and counter-radicalisation efforts.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We hope that more Singaporeans can come onboard this journey and play a part.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Most importantly, look out for your family members, look out for your children because today, our children spend a lot of time online and you never know what they come across because self-radicalisation is a process.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: For some, it can happen quickly, for others, it is a process and it is a journey, but we want their journey to be a positive one and a healthy one.
